title: Dispatch LTP 6: Editor Publishes the Paper’s Contradictory Futures
summary: Readers are shown what changed and asked to stop seeking tomorrow’s issue.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: The Chronicle yesterday printed the original advance account of the East Bridge beside its rewritten version. Mr. Ashcombe added a signed explanation of the crane, streetcar, and warehouse reports. He asked readers to bring any early copies to the office without passing them onward.

The appeal has produced fifty-three papers from homes around Alderwick. Some carry articles the office has never received. One says the Chronicle’s doors will close before the month ends. Another describes the editor ordering a press dismantled while a crowd waits in the street. Neither gives a cause.

Miss Marsh and Dr. Saye found a second impression beneath the pressroom floor. An obsolete iron type forme, stored there since a former owner’s time, holds blank strips where headlines should be. Each morning, the strips show shallow indentations in the shape of words from the next day’s advance issue. By the time the bundle arrives, the indentations have deepened.

The forme cannot account by ordinary means for papers delivered across the city, but its surface is bound to the same changing headlines. Dr. Saye thinks printing, reading, and expectation are completing a circuit through the Eidetic Stratum. She urges the editor to stop operating the press until the forme can be removed.

Mr. Ashcombe has refused an immediate closure. Staff wages and public notices depend on tomorrow’s run. “We can’t ask people to stop reading their own newspaper,” he said. He has instead ordered the old forme guarded and locked away from the press.
